governingStatute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (Act No. 12 of 2017)
title: Eligibility and conditions for taking input tax credit and mandatory 180-day payment rule

effectivePeriod.annualReset: Every November 30 (Statutory ITC cutoff deadline under Section 16(4))
effectivePeriod.sunsetNotes: Active statutory framework amended by Finance Act 2021 (clause aa w.e.f. 01-01-2022), Finance Act 2022 (clause ba and Nov 30 cutoff w.e.f. 01-10-2022), and Finance (No. 2) Act 2024 (subsections 5 & 6 retrospective relief).

plainTextSummary: Under Section 16(2) of the CGST Act, 2017, no registered person is entitled to input tax credit (ITC) on any supply of goods or services unless five cumulative statutory conditions are met: (a) Possession of a tax invoice or debit note issued by a registered supplier under Section 31; (aa) Details of the invoice/debit note have been furnished by the supplier in the statement of outward supplies under Section 37 (GSTR-1) and communicated to the recipient in the manner specified under Section 38 (auto-drafted in GSTR-2B); (b) Recipient has received the goods or services or both (including 'bill-to-ship-to' deemed receipt under Explanation); (ba) Details of ITC communicated under Section 38 have not been restricted; (c) Tax charged has been actually paid to the Government, either in cash or through utilization of admissible ITC; (d) Return under Section 39 (GSTR-3B) has been furnished. Second Proviso (180-Day Rule): Where a recipient fails to pay the supplier the amount towards the value of supply along with tax payable within 180 days from the invoice date, an amount equal to the ITC availed must be paid by the recipient along with interest under Section 50, reported in Table 4(B)(2) of GSTR-3B under Rule 37. Third Proviso: The recipient is entitled to re-avail such ITC in Table 4(A)(5) and Table 4(D)(1) upon subsequent payment of the invoice amount to the supplier. Statutory Exceptions to 180-Day Rule: Does not apply to supplies where tax is payable on reverse charge basis under Section 9(3)/9(4), deemed supplies without consideration under Schedule I, or additions to value under Section 15(2)(b). Relationship to Section 16(4): Section 16(4) establishes an annual cutoff deadline (30th November following the financial year or filing of annual return under Section 44, whichever is earlier), subject to retrospective statutory relief under subsections (5) and (6) for FY 2017-18 through 2020-21.

mandatoryEligibilityConditions: 16(2)(a): Possession of valid Tax Invoice / Debit Note under Section 31
16(2)(aa): Supplier reporting in GSTR-1 (Section 37) and communication in GSTR-2B (Section 38)
16(2)(b): Actual or deemed constructive receipt of goods or services
16(2)(ba): Input tax credit not restricted in Section 38 communication
16(2)(c): Tax charged actually discharged by supplier to Government
16(2)(d): Furnishing of valid GSTR-3B return under Section 39
statutoryReversalExceptions: Supplies on which tax is payable under Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM) under Section 9(3) or Section 9(4)
Deemed supplies without consideration under Schedule I of the CGST Act
Amounts added to value of supply on account of supplier's liability incurred by recipient under Section 15(2)(b)
keyStatutoryThresholds.annualCutoffDeadline: 30th November following the end of the financial year to which the invoice pertains, or date of filing Annual Return (GSTR-9), whichever is earlier (Section 16(4) as amended by Finance Act, 2022 w.e.f. 01-10-2022)
keyStatutoryThresholds.retrospectiveReliefProvisions: Section 16(5) & Section 16(6) inserted by Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 provide retrospective extension for invoices pertaining to FY 2017-18, 2018-19, 2019-20, and 2020-21 where GSTR-3B was filed up to 30th November 2021.
